back: An intense rotating low-pressure storm over warm tropical seas; hurricane (Atlantic), typhoon (NW Pacific), cyclone (Indian Ocean).
About 5° to 20-30° N and S, over seas of about 26.5 °C or more; not on the equator (Coriolis too weak).
Warm moist air rises → condensation releases latent heat → air rises faster → more air drawn in and spins.
Eye (calm, sinking air), eye wall (strongest winds, heaviest rain), spiral rain bands, cirrus outflow.
A rise in sea level above the normal tide caused by onshore winds and very low pressure.
Strong winds, storm surge, torrential rain, floods, landslides; then disease and food shortages.
March 2019: landfall near Beira; floods and landslides in Chimanimani and Chipinge; more than 1,000 deaths across three countries.
No warm sea to supply heat and moisture; friction slows the winds.
